key_insight: FCV-PICRN reconstructs flow structures inside unsupervised gaps by combining Fourier features, complex-valued learning, and Navier–Stokes constraints.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help recover velocity, pressure, and vorticity from incomplete, noisy flow measurements when sensors miss dynamically important regions.
method: Fourier features encode oscillatory and multiscale flow structures.
Complex-valued representations support coupled amplitude–phase learning.
Convolutional residual blocks enforce Navier–Stokes physics.
evidence_signal: Tests cover Taylor–Green and cylinder-wake flows at Re=100, three severe wake-gap geometries, Gaussian and speckle noise, and forced 2D Kolmogorov turbulence, where reconstruction errors were lower than a conventional PINN with 5% Gaussian noise.
watch_item: Validation is limited to the reported 2D cases; performance on 3D, higher-Reynolds-number flows and computational cost remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: Fourier-Feature-Embedded Complex-Valued Physics-Informed Convolutional Residual Networks for Sparse and Gappy Noisy Flow-Field Reconstruction
